CONTENTS
  1. What drives the camera (scripts, objects, Camera component, Cinemachine status)
  2. The per-frame algorithm, step by step, with this scene's numbers

  5. Every CameraParentRotator parameter: current value, what it does, what happens when raised / lowered

================================================================================================
1. WHAT DRIVES THE CAMERA
================================================================================================

1.1 Objects in the scene (Assets/MainScene prop camera 3.unity)
  CameraParent                       (empty object; THE RIG - this is what moves and yaws)
    components: Transform, CameraParentRotator (enabled), DebugTimeScale (enabled, slowDown = OFF, timeScale 0.3 unused)
    Transform scale 1. It carries the camera YAW only. Position = focus - forward * boom.
    └ Main Camera                    (child; carries the TILT only)
        local position (0,0,0) (+ optional shake offset), local rotation (35.264, 0, 0)
        components: Transform, Camera, AudioListener, PostProcessLayer (legacy post-processing),
                    UniversalAdditionalCameraData (URP)
  Parent * child = Euler(35.264, yaw, 0) exactly, so the isometric tilt cannot drift.

1.2 Camera component values (scene as authored)
  Projection                orthographic = true     (so FOV 60 is stored but unused)
  Orthographic Size         22   (authored; the rig treats it as a FLOOR - see minOrthoSize / MinFrameSize)
  Near / Far clip           0.3 / 200
  Clear flags               2 (solid colour)  background (0.173, 0.165, 0.141)
  Depth                     -1,  culling mask Everything,  viewport rect 0,0,1,1
  HDR true,  MSAA allowed true,  occlusion culling true,  dynamic resolution false
  Tag                       MainCamera
  URP data                  renderer index 1 (Settings/PropLooks_Renderer, Default Forward + SSAO),
                            post-processing ON, shadows ON, antialiasing 1 (FXAA), depth/colour texture options 2 (use pipeline setting)
  Game view used for the recording: 750 x 1334 portrait  ->  aspect = 0.5622
      (the rig reads boomCamera.aspect every frame; if it is not available it assumes 9/19.5 = 0.4615)
  A camera that sits 60-63 units from its focus with far clip 200 sees 140+ units behind the focus: nothing is clipped.

1.3 Cinemachine
  The Cinemachine package (com.unity.cinemachine 3.1.6) is INSTALLED in the project (Packages/manifest.json) but this scene
  contains ZERO Cinemachine components: no CinemachineBrain, no virtual cameras, no Body/Aim/Extension, no blends.
  The only scene in the project that references Cinemachine is "New Scene.unity". So there are no Cinemachine values to tune here.
  Everything is custom code in CameraParentRotator. For orientation, the closest Cinemachine equivalents are:
      Cinemachine concept                  -> this rig
      Follow target + Body damping         -> followPlayer (how much) + followSmoothTime (how lazily)
      Framing Transposer dead / soft zone  -> softFrameLimit (comfort box) and hardFrameLimit (never-leave box)
      Group Composer / target group        -> the "must see" list: runner + look-ahead cubes (lookAheadCubes, lookAheadCorners, lookAheadMaxCubes)
      Lens > Ortho Size                    -> orthographic size built from zoomShown, zoomOutMultiplier, boost, speed zoom
      Brain blend (custom ease)            -> Transitioning state: SmootherStep between two solved shots (transitionDuration...)
      Shot / Priority switching            -> zones: one solved shot per zone, switched when the runner nears the zone's end
      Confiner / Collider                  -> none
      Noise / Impulse                      -> flip shake + punch (disabled, flipImpactEnabled = False)

1.4 Scripts that move or influence the camera (all under Assets/)
  WRITES THE CAMERA
    Scripts/CameraParentRotator.cs    The only script that writes CameraParent position/yaw, Main Camera tilt and orthographicSize
                                      every frame (LateUpdate). Everything below only feeds it, reads it, or pauses it.
    PlayerController.cs (CubeRailRunner)   On a soft restart it glides the camera back to the opening shot for 0.4 s (ease-out cubic):
                                      rig.SnapToPlayerZone() computes the target pose, then the camera is lerped there by hand.
    Scripts/GameOverSequence.cs       0.2 s after the runner dies it DISABLES CameraParentRotator (camera freezes, "stays put and watches");
                                      UnfreezeCamera() re-enables it on restart.
    Scripts/TutorialManager.cs        Tutorial scene only: rig.SnapToPlayerZone() (not used in this scene).
    Scripts/DebugTimeScale.cs         On CameraParent. slowDown = OFF here, so Time.timeScale is untouched. (If ticked: game runs at 0.3x.)
  FEEDS THE CAMERA (inputs it reads)
    Scripts/DynamicPathGenerator*.cs  Builds the track, groups legs into ZONES (= camera shots), plans the camera yaws (PlanCameraYaws),
                                      solves each shot (PathZone.SolveFraming), answers GetPathAhead / IsPlayerNearZoneEnd / GetZoneAfter /
                                      PlayerProgressThrough, owns the boost-zoom values, culls old zones.
    Scripts/Difficulty/DifficultyProfile.cs  (asset Assets/Difficulty/MainScenePropCamera2_Difficulty.asset, assigned on this scene's generator)
                                      cameraOverrides = ON: overrides boostCameraZoomOut / InSeconds / OutSeconds and caps the rig's speedZoomMax.
                                      restrictCameraRotation = ON: the camera may only change yaw into zones whose first leg is a RELEASE-phase leg
                                      (legs 0-5 of each 30-leg portal cycle) or a portal runway. Also shapes leg lengths (time budget) and speed.
    Scripts/PathDepthShading.cs       Decides how many legs are DRAWN ahead/behind; exposes VisibleAheadCubes which the rig reads.
    PlayerController.cs               Runner position and forwardSpeed (follow target, hand-over timing, speed zoom, lead).
  READS THE CAMERA (no effect on where it points)
    PlayerController.cs  (cameraRig.SettledViewRotation -> which on-screen side left/right controls map to; TriggerFlipImpact on a double-tap flip)
    TrialMonument/Scripts/PortalZoneController.cs (turns the door billboards toward camera.forward), Scripts/NeonWindowDecorator.cs
    (EnsureZoneSolved: asks where a zone's shot will stand), TrialMonument/Scripts/MonumentSkyBackdrop.cs (sizes the sky quad from the camera's
    ortho size), Scripts/RunnerBoostFX.cs (faces the glow quad to the camera), Scripts/AutoPlayer.cs, MockHumanPlayer.cs, TmpCamRecorder.cs.
  NOT PRESENT IN THIS SCENE
    Scripts/PathVisualTuner.cs (in-game slider panel; it would only touch zoomOutMultiplier) - not in this scene.
    Scripts/SmoothPathCameraPivot.cs - not used. Scripts/TrialCameraControls.cs - not on this camera.

1.5 Update order
  Rig = CameraParentRotator.LateUpdate (default execution order 0). PathDepthShading has [DefaultExecutionOrder(50)] and also runs in LateUpdate,
  i.e. AFTER the rig. So the rig reads VisibleAheadCubes from the PREVIOUS frame (a one-frame lag; harmless).
  The recording was taken in Application.onBeforeRender, i.e. after every LateUpdate: the values in the log are the final pose that was drawn.


================================================================================================
2. THE PER-FRAME ALGORITHM (CameraParentRotator.LateUpdate), with this scene's numbers
================================================================================================

LateUpdate():
  a) PlanIfStale()      - if the generator added track (pathGenerationCount changed) re-run PlanCameraYaws for all sealed zones ahead.
  b) switch(state)      - Static -> TickStatic()   (hold timer, watch for the cue to move)
                          Transitioning -> TickTransition()   (SmootherStep from shot A to shot B)
  c) UpdateLean()       - only in Static: turn a few degrees toward the next shot's yaw.
  d) ApplyPose()        - builds the final pose from: shot + follow + lean + keep-in-frame, sets zoom, writes the transforms.

ApplyPose(), in order (this is the part that produces every number in the log):
  0. yaw  = baseYaw + lean.   rot = Euler(35.264, yaw, 0).   right/up/forward = rot * axes.
  1. FOLLOW.   followTarget = ( (runner - baseFocus) projected on right/up ) * followPlayer           [followPlayer 0.45]
               followOffset = SmoothDamp(followOffset -> followTarget, time = followSmoothTime)       [0.15 s]
               focus = baseFocus + right*follow.x + up*follow.y
               NOTE: followTarget is measured from baseFocus, i.e. from the CENTRE OF THE CURRENT SHOT. When the shot changes (a camera move),
               baseFocus jumps toward the next zone's centre, so the follow target changes sign/size at once and the offset swings to the new
               value within ~0.15-0.5 s. In the recording the follow offset flipped sign during moves (e.g. move 1: (-2.98, 1.79) -> (3.36, -2.05)).
  2. MUST-SEE BOX.  CollectMustSee() builds a list of points the camera must keep on screen: the runner plus the path ahead
               (see section 4), projected onto the camera's right/up axes relative to focus, padded by 0.75 world units (half a cube + air).
               The look-ahead box's size is eased (extentSmoothTime 0.35 s); because smoothLookAheadCenter is ON its CENTRE is damped separately
               (lookAheadCenterSmoothTime 0.6 s). The runner is added AFTER the smoothing, exact, so the runner can never be smoothed off screen.
  3. ZOOM.     (fitZoomToVisibleTrack = ON in this scene)
               spanHalfH = max( (maxY-minY)/2 , (maxX-minX)/2/aspect )              <- how much half-height the box needs
               fit       = max( spanHalfH / softFrameLimit , MinFrameSize )         <- MinFrameSize = max(minOrthoSize 22, authored 22) = 22
               zoomPeak  = max(fit, zoomPeak - zoomTightenPerSecond*dt)             <- widens at once, tightens at most 6 units/s
               zoomShown = SmoothDamp(zoomShown -> zoomPeak, time = 0.25 s when widening (zoomSmoothTime*0.5), 0.5 s when tightening)
               ortho     = max(zoomShown, spanHalfH / hardFrameLimit) * zoomOutMultiplier                     [x1.05]
               then   ortho *= boostZoom          (1.0 -> 1.15 on a zig-zag boost, linear MoveTowards: 0.5 s in, 0.4 s out)
                      ortho *= speedZoom          (1.0 -> up to 1.15, scaled by runner speed between its start speed and maxSpeed 33, SmoothDamp 1.5 s)
                      ortho  = max(ortho * punch, spanHalfH/hard)   (punch disabled: punchAmount 0, flipImpactEnabled false)
               In this scene: baseline = 22 x 1.05 = 23.1  (the log's 23.1 at the start), 23.3-23.8 as speed zoom creeps in, ~27 during a boost.
               IMPORTANT: with fitZoomToVisibleTrack ON the zone's own solved ortho size (optimalOrthoSize, 35..89 in the log) is NOT what is rendered.
               baseOrtho / maxZoomInPerShot / framingPadding only matter when fitZoomToVisibleTrack is OFF. The rendered zoom comes from the look-ahead box.
  4. SLIDE (keep-in-frame).   halfW = ortho*aspect,  halfH = ortho.
               softTarget = the smallest shift that puts the whole box inside the SOFT box (softFrameLimit 0.85 of the half-screen)
               frameShift = SmoothDamp(frameShift -> softTarget, time = keepInFrameSmoothTime 0.15 s)
               hardBoxSpring ON (this scene): the smooth time slides from 0.15 s at the soft limit down to hardSpringFastSmoothTime 0.05 s as the content
               approaches the hard limit (hardFrameLimit 0.88) - a progressive rubber band. The instant "hard clamp" is skipped in this mode.
               (hardBoxSpring OFF: after the eased slide the hard box is enforced with no smoothing = the camera can snap. That is the old behaviour.)
  5. POSE.     focus += right*frameShift.x + up*frameShift.y
               CameraParent.position = focus - forward * baseBoom            (baseBoom 60, up to 63+ for big zones)
               CameraParent.rotation = Euler(0, yaw, 0)       Main Camera.localRotation = Euler(35.264, 0, 0)
               Main Camera.localPosition = shake offset (0 - shake disabled)    Main Camera.orthographicSize = ortho

So the camera's final position is:   shot centre (baseFocus)  +  follow (0.45 x runner offset, 0.15 s lag)  +  keep-in-frame slide  -  forward*boom
and its size is:                     max(22, look-ahead-fit) x 1.05 x boost(1..1.15) x speed(1..1.15)


================================================================================================
3. WHEN IT DECIDES TO MOVE / ROTATE / FOLLOW / FRAME
================================================================================================

3.1 Where "shots" come from: ZONES
  The generator groups consecutive legs into ZONES. One zone = one held camera shot. The camera moves when the runner reaches the end of a zone.
  Zone size (OpenZone):  capacity = clamp( max( random(minSegmentsPerZone 2 .. maxSegmentsPerZone 3),  ceil(targetZoneSeconds 5 / secondsPerLeg) ),
                                           2 .. max(3, maxSegmentsPerZoneCap 6) )
  With legs that take ~1.1-1.5 s to cross, ceil(5/1.3) = 4 -> zones are typically 3-4 legs, ~5 s each. That is why the recording shows a camera move
  about every 4 points of score (score 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 24).
  Hand-off overlap: each new zone's bounds are seeded with the previous zone's FINAL segment, and the previous zone is stretched over the new zone's
  FIRST segment (ExtendPreviousZoneOverHandover), so consecutive shots share their junction and the runner stays inside both during the move.
  SolveFraming (per zone): rotates the zone's 8 bounding-box corners into camera space for the chosen yaw, takes the projected box centre as
  optimalFocus (= where the camera looks), optimalOrthoSize = max(vertical half-extent, horizontal half-extent/aspect) + framingPadding (>= minOrtho),
  optimalBoom = max(boomDistance, bounds.extents.magnitude + 10). Once the camera commits to a zone (LockFraming) these numbers are frozen.

3.2 Choosing the yaw (rotation): PlanCameraYaws, run for ALL sealed zones ahead whenever track is added
  Each zone has 4 candidate yaws = snapped average heading + 0/90/180/270 + isoYawOffset 45 => the four isometric yaws 45/135/225/315.
  Score of a candidate (ScoreYaw, lower is better) = 1.5 x (number of cube pairs that overlap on screen but are far apart in depth)
                                                      + 0.5 x (cubes running TOWARD the camera).      (compactness is deliberately NOT scored)
  A Viterbi search then picks one yaw per zone minimising  sum(scores) + angleChangeCost (11) per 90 degrees changed (a 180 costs 4x = 44).
  So the camera keeps its yaw across several zones and turns in 90 degree steps only when the legibility gain beats 11 points.
  Extra gate in this scene: DifficultyProfile.restrictCameraRotation = ON -> a zone may only be entered with a different yaw if its first leg is in
  the RELEASE phase (cycle legs 0-5 of each 30-leg cycle) or is a portal runway; otherwise +100000 cost = forbidden.
  Zone-door (portal) zones force their yaw (forcedYaw) so the door faces the camera. In the recording the yaw stayed 315 the whole time (6 moves, all pans).

3.3 STATE: Static (holding a shot)  -  TickStatic every frame
  holdTimer += dt
  1. If there is no current zone / it was culled: adopt the runner's zone immediately (a cut, no travel).
  2. If holdTimer < minHoldSeconds (2.5 s): do nothing. A shot that just landed is held even if the runner is already leaving it; follow + keep-in-frame
     keep the runner on screen meanwhile. (Log phase label: HOLD)
  3. If the runner's zone is not the camera's zone (runner outran the shot): BeginTransition(runner's zone) at once.
  4. lead = transitionLeadSegments (0) + (speedScaledLead ON) round( lerp(0, leadMaxExtraSegments 2, speedFraction) ), speedFraction =
     (forwardSpeed - startSpeed) / (maxSpeed 33 - startSpeed).  Effective lead: 0 below ~17.2 u/s, 1 from ~17.2 to ~28, 2 above ~28 u/s.
     In the recording the runner never exceeded 16.7 u/s, so the lead was 0 for all 6 moves.
  5. If the runner is within `lead` segments of the end of the camera's zone (IsPlayerNearZoneEnd; with lead 0 = the runner stands on the zone's LAST leg)
     and a next zone exists: BeginTransition(next zone).   (Log phase label: ARMED while waiting for this)
  While static, every frame ApplyPose still moves the camera through FOLLOW (steps 1 above), KEEP-IN-FRAME SLIDE, LEAN and ZOOM. A "static" shot is
  therefore never frozen: the camera drifts at roughly 0.45 x the runner's speed (measured ~0.4 average, 5-6 u/s) plus slide corrections.

3.4 LEAN (Static only)
  If inPlaceLeanDegrees > 0 and the NEXT shot's yaw differs, the camera yaw is turned toward it by up to inPlaceLeanDegrees (5) x the runner's progress
  through the zone (PlayerProgressThrough 0..1), SmoothDamp leanSmoothTime (0.8 s). When the next yaw is the same (as in this recording) lean stays 0.
  At BeginTransition lean is folded into the starting yaw and reset to 0 so the move continues from what is on screen.

3.5 BeginTransition(next)
  - Solve the next shot. If its focus is more than snapDistance (200) from the current focus: CUT (adopt) instead of travelling.
  - Start values: fromFocus = baseFocus, fromYaw = baseYaw + lean, fromOrtho = baseOrtho, fromBoom = baseBoom.
  - activeTargetOrtho = max(next.optimalOrthoSize, fromOrtho * (1 - maxZoomInPerShot 0.12))       (only matters for baseOrtho; see zoom note above)
  - Duration:  timed = matchTransitionToRunner ? clamp( distance(runner -> end of the zone's final segment) / forwardSpeed , minTransitionDuration 0.6 ,
                                                          transitionDuration 1.2 ) : 1.2
               quarters = |angle change| / 90
               duration = max( timed , minTransitionDuration 0.6 + quarters x secondsPer90Degrees 0.7 )
               => a straight pan: 0.6-1.2 s (the recording: 1.03-1.21 s).  A 90 degree turn: >= 1.3 s.  A 180: >= 2.0 s.
  - next.LockFraming(): the destination is frozen, so later planning cannot move it mid-flight.
  - state = Transitioning.

3.6 STATE: Transitioning  -  TickTransition every frame
  t = SmootherStep( transitionTimer / duration )         (6t^5 - 15t^4 + 10t^3: zero speed AND zero acceleration at both ends)
  baseFocus = Lerp(fromFocus, target.optimalFocus, t)     baseYaw = LerpAngle(fromYaw, target.optimalCameraYaw, t)
  baseOrtho = Lerp(fromOrtho, activeTargetOrtho, t)       baseBoom = max(fromBoom, target.optimalBoom)   <- NOT eased: it steps at the first frame
  Peak speed of a SmootherStep is 1.875 x the average speed. A 22-unit shot move in 1.2 s averages 18 u/s and peaks at ~34 u/s; a 54-unit move in 1.03 s peaks ~98 u/s of SHOT motion.
  Follow, keep-in-frame slide and the zoom fit keep running on top of the move the whole time (they are never paused).
  At t = 1: FinishTransition -> currentZone = target; AdoptZone(resetMotion=false) so follow/slide keep their values; holdTimer = 0 (the 2.5 s hold restarts);
  baseBoom snaps to the zone's own boom.

3.7 Other ways the camera jumps or is replaced
  - Restart after death: rig.SnapToPlayerZone() then a hand-made 0.4 s ease-out glide from the frozen pose to the opening shot (PlayerController).
  - Game over: the rig is disabled 0.2 s after death, the camera stays where it is. Re-enabled on restart.
  - Path regenerated / zone culled from under the camera: TickStatic re-adopts the runner's zone (a cut). Teleport > snapDistance 200: cut.
  - Zone doors (portals): the generator forces the camera yaw for the two door zones (portalCameraYawOffset 45 must equal isoYawOffset).


================================================================================================
4. WHAT THE CAMERA IS SUPPOSED TO SHOW - LEGS AHEAD / BEHIND / CURRENT
================================================================================================

Three different things decide what is on screen. They are NOT the same number:

A) WHAT IS DRAWN (PathDepthShading, "Visible Window")
     limitVisibleLegs = ON
     visibleLegsAhead  = 3   -> the leg the runner is on  +  the next 3 legs are drawn (fading in over the last edgeFadeCubes 5 cubes; a new leg
                                draws itself in at revealCubesPerSecond 45). A zone door ahead also shows the runway out of it and the legs laid beyond it.
                                A boost under way is drawn to its end, however many legs.
     visibleLegsBehind = 2   -> the 2 legs before the runner's stay drawn, plus the part of the current leg already crossed. Older cubes disappear
                                at hideCubesPerSecond 60, fading over behindFadeOutCubes 5. The runner's trail is cut to end where the last drawn cube ends.
     So, by design, the player sees ~ 2 behind + current + 3 ahead = about 6 legs of track in the world, but the camera is only OBLIGED to frame part of that.

B) WHAT THE CAMERA MUST KEEP ON SCREEN EVERY FRAME ("must-see" box, CollectMustSee / pathGen.GetPathAhead)
     - the RUNNER (exact).
     - the cubes ahead of the runner, starting at the cube nearest the runner, in route order:
           minCount = max( lookAheadCubes 10 , ceil( min( VisibleAheadCubes , lookAheadMaxCubes 20 ) ) )
           it keeps adding cubes past minCount until `lookAheadCorners` (2) corners have been passed,
           BUT never more than lookAheadMaxCubes (20) cubes in total.
     - NOTHING behind the runner is required (only the runner itself). Track behind can scroll off the bottom.
   Result in numbers: legs are 12-25 cubes long at the speeds seen here (time-budget legs: ~1.0-1.3 s at 11.9-19 u/s; the authored legTiers 14-18 / 16-22 / 19-28 /
   22-34 apply when the time budget is off). A 20-cube cap is therefore only about ONE leg and a bit: the rest of the leg the runner is on plus the start of the
   next. The "2 corners" rule almost never gets satisfied before the 20-cube cap cuts it off.
   >>> ANSWER: There is NO rule in the code that says "always show the next 2 legs". The guarantee is cube-count based: >= 10 cubes (up to 20 when more track is
   >>> drawn) and the camera stops caring after 20 cubes. With 14-25 cube legs, the camera only guarantees the CURRENT leg's remainder plus roughly the start of the
   >>> NEXT leg (and the next corner when it is within 20 cubes). Legs 2 and 3 ahead are drawn but can sit outside the screen.
   >>> To guarantee 2 full legs ahead you would need lookAheadMaxCubes >= about 2 x the longest leg (40-50) and lookAheadCubes of the same order; the cost is that the
   >>> must-see box grows, so the zoom-out fit (spanHalfH / softFrameLimit) rises above the 22 floor and the runner gets smaller.
     (The recording's "ext" column is that box: minX,maxX,minY,maxY relative to the focus, in world units along the camera's right/up axes.)

C) WHAT THE SHOT (ZONE) CONTAINS
     A zone = capacity 2-6 legs (typically 3-4 here: targetZoneSeconds 5), plus the overlap with the previous zone's last leg and the next zone's first leg.
     The camera travels to the CENTRE of that box. But with fitZoomToVisibleTrack ON the zone's size does not set the zoom, so a 4-leg zone (up to ~90 world units
     long) is centred but not necessarily fully visible; what is guaranteed visible is box B.
     Legs generated ahead of the runner (not drawn / not framed): minSegmentsAhead 6 legs always built ahead; minZonesAhead 2 sealed zones queued; the camera plan
     (yaws) is solved over all of them; zonesToKeepBehind 5 zones are kept before their cubes are destroyed.

Geometry, to judge what fits (game view 750x1334, aspect 0.5622):
     ortho 23.1  ->  visible height 46.2 world units, width 26.0.   Soft box (0.85): +-11.0 wide, +-19.6 tall.  Hard box (0.88): +-11.4 wide, +-20.3 tall.
     In the isometric view a cube step along a ground axis moves 0.707 right and 0.408 up on screen (45 degree yaw, 35.264 tilt); a step up/down moves 0.816 on screen.
     A 16-cube leg therefore spans about 11.3 wide x 6.5 tall on screen; 20 cubes = 14 x 8.2. A leg that runs left-to-right can fill half the screen width by itself.


================================================================================================
5. EVERY CameraParentRotator PARAMETER   (current value = value logged in the header of the recording)
   format:  name = current   [range]   what it does.  UP: ...   DOWN: ...
================================================================================================

--- Locked isometric angle ---
isometricTiltX = 35.264   Camera pitch. 35.264 = atan(1/sqrt2) = true isometric. Held EXACTLY every frame.
    UP:   looks more top-down; ground tracks get taller on screen, vertical legs shorter. DOWN: flatter, more side-on; track compresses vertically.
    Changes all screen geometry AND the left/right control mapping (SettledViewRotation). Leave at 35.264.
isoYawOffset = 45   Added to the snapped zone heading. With quantiseZoneYaw it gives the four yaws 45/135/225/315, so legs recede on the diagonal and the inner corner of
    every turn is open. Other values break the symmetric diagonal look. portalCameraYawOffset on the generator must match it (45).
quantiseZoneYaw = True   Snap the zone's average heading to 90 degrees before adding the offset.
    OFF: yaw follows the raw average heading -> arbitrary angles, yaw differs from zone to zone, many more/odd rotations.

--- Choosing the angle ---
angleChangeCost = 11   [0..30]   Cost of one 90 degree change in the Viterbi yaw plan (180 degrees = 4x).
    UP: camera keeps the same yaw for longer, turns only when the track ahead is really hard to read. DOWN: turns more often; 0 = every zone takes its own best yaw.
    (In this scene it is further limited by restrictCameraRotation - the camera can only turn into RELEASE-phase zones.)

--- Zone framing (solving each shot) ---
framingPadding = 3   World units of slack around the zone box when computing optimalOrthoSize.
    Practically NO visible effect while fitZoomToVisibleTrack is ON (the zone's ortho is not rendered). If fit zoom were OFF: UP = wider shots.
minOrthoSize = 22   Floor on the solved size AND (as MinFrameSize = max(minOrthoSize, the Camera's own orthographic size 22)) the floor of the rendered fit-zoom.
    UP: the whole game is framed wider (runner smaller) and zoom pumps less. DOWN: cannot go below the Camera component's 22 (it is a max of both) - the authored 22 is
    the floor (user preference: do not frame tighter than the authored zoom).
boomDistance = 60   How far the camera sits back from the focus along the view axis. Orthographic: the picture size does NOT change with it; it only decides clipping
    (near 0.3 / far 200) and depth for fog/backdrop. The solver raises it for large zones: optimalBoom = max(60, extents.magnitude + 10) (62.88 for the big zone in move 6).
    A change of boom moves the camera along its view axis in ONE frame at a hand-off (see 3.6) - it shows as a position step in the log but no change of framing.

--- Zone transition (the move between two shots) ---
transitionDuration = 1.2   [seconds]  Ceiling on a move timed to the runner. UP: slower, softer pans (less speed). DOWN: snappier, faster pans (more speed).
matchTransitionToRunner = True   Move time = remaining time for the runner to clear the zone (clamped min..max above). OFF: always transitionDuration.
minTransitionDuration = 0.6   Floor on any move. UP: every move is slower. DOWN: lets a very short hand-over make a very quick move.
transitionLeadSegments = 0   [0..3]  How many legs before the zone's end the move starts. 0 = when the runner is on the zone's last leg.
    UP: the move starts earlier (more time, gentler for the same distance) but the camera leaves the zone while the runner is still inside it; keep-in-frame must hold them.
    DOWN: later start, moves compressed into the last leg (what the log shows: 1.0-1.2 s).
snapDistance = 200   Shot-to-shot distance above which the camera CUTS instead of travelling (regeneration / teleports). Lower: cuts for long legit moves too (the longest here was 54).
minHoldSeconds = 2.5   [0..10]  Least time a landed shot is held before another move may begin. UP: fewer, larger moves; if the runner outruns the shot, one forced move happens later.
    DOWN: moves may come back to back. (With ~5 s zones this value is below the zone time so it rarely decides; with short zones it would.)
maxZoomInPerShot = 0.12   [0..0.5]  Most the shot's base zoom may tighten per hand-off. Only affects baseOrtho - NOT the rendered zoom while fitZoomToVisibleTrack is ON.
secondsPer90Degrees = 0.7   [0..5]  Extra seconds a move takes per 90 degrees of rotation. UP: slower turns. DOWN: faster, snappier turns (more yaw speed).
    A 90 degree turn lasts max(timed, 0.6 + 0.7) = 1.3 s; 180 degrees 2.0 s.

--- Follow & lean ---
followPlayer = 0.45   [0..1]  Share of the runner's offset from the shot centre that the camera takes on. 0 = fully locked diorama, 1 = runner kept dead centre.
    UP: camera tracks the runner more closely (runner stays central, world scrolls less relative to the runner; camera moves faster in static phases).
    DOWN: calmer, the camera barely moves while a shot is held and the runner crosses the screen instead (but the runner reaches the soft/hard box sooner and keep-in-frame must slide).
    Because the target is relative to the SHOT CENTRE, the follow value reverses at every hand-off (see 2.1 and section 7).
followSmoothTime = 0.15   [seconds]  Follow SmoothDamp time. UP: lazier, camera lags the runner more, more slide work for keep-in-frame. DOWN: nearly rigid follow; hand-off reversals complete quicker.
inPlaceLeanDegrees = 5   [0..20]  Degrees the camera turns in place toward the next shot's yaw during a hold. 0 = never. UP: more pre-rotation (the later move has less to rotate) but more visible sway while holding.
leanSmoothTime = 0.8   Seconds the lean takes to settle. UP: slower sway. DOWN: faster.

--- Keep path in frame ---
lookAheadCubes = 10   [0..40]  Fewest cubes ahead of the runner that must be on screen with the runner. UP: wider box -> zoom-out above 22 sooner/pan to include more track. DOWN: shows less ahead.
lookAheadCorners = 2   [0..4]  Keep adding cubes until this many turns have been passed (but never beyond lookAheadMaxCubes). 0 = just the cube count.
lookAheadMaxCubes = 20   [10..120]  Ceiling on the look-ahead (cubes). THE number that decides how much of the next legs is guaranteed (20 cubes ~ 1.2 legs here).
    UP: more of the next legs guaranteed in frame, but bigger box = more zoom-out and stronger pans toward the corner. DOWN: less guaranteed, tighter, runner larger.
extentSmoothTime = 0.35   [0..1.5]  Seconds the look-ahead box SIZE is eased over (it changes cube by cube and jumps a whole leg at each corner). 0 = raw (can pop).
    UP: smoother but slower to react to a new corner. DOWN: snappier, more step motion.
softFrameLimit = 0.85   [0.3..0.95]  Share of the half-screen the must-see box may reach before the camera slides to bring it back (the comfort box). Also divides the zoom fit.
    UP: camera tolerates content nearer the screen edge (less sliding, but zoom-fit gets tighter and track sits near the edge). DOWN: camera acts earlier, keeps more margin (more movement, wider zoom).
hardFrameLimit = 0.88   [0.5..0.98]  Share of the half-screen NEVER allowed to be passed (the guarantee). Here only 0.03 above the soft limit = a very thin comfort band: the soft slide and the
    hard spring are almost the same box, so corrections arrive quickly. UP: closer to the edge allowed. DOWN: stronger guarantee, more correction.
keepInFrameSmoothTime = 0.5 default -> 0.15 here   Seconds the comfort slide takes to settle. UP: slower slide (more time with content near the edge). DOWN: snappier, more visible correction movement.
zoomOutMultiplier = 1.05   [0.6..2.5]  Final zoom multiplier, applied last (hard limit still holds). 1 = as fitted. UP: wider view (runner smaller; more track visible both ahead and behind). DOWN: tighter.
    Together with the 22 floor the resting ortho is 22 x 1.05 = 23.1.
fitZoomToVisibleTrack = True   Zoom follows the look-ahead box (not the zone). OFF: zoom = zone ortho + extra (only ever widens), which is the older, pumping behaviour.
zoomSmoothTime = 0.5   [0.2..6]  Seconds the zoom takes to settle (widening uses half of it). UP: slower, calmer zoom (but the hard limit still snaps wider if needed). DOWN: quicker zoom.
zoomTightenPerSecond = 6   [0.2..10]  Fastest the zoom may TIGHTEN (ortho units/s). UP: zoom returns quickly after a wide moment. DOWN: view stays wide longer, less pumping. (Widening is not limited.)

--- Speed zoom (opt-in) ---
speedZoomEnabled = True   Widen the zoom as the runner gets faster.
speedZoomMax = 1.15 (scene) , capped by the profile to 1.15   [1..2]  Zoom factor at the runner's max speed (33). Actual factor = 1 + (max-1) x speedFraction. In this recording it only reached ~1.03-1.05.
speedZoomSmoothTime = 1.5   Seconds to catch up. UP: gentler. DOWN: faster, noticeable.

--- Hard box spring (opt-in) ---
hardBoxSpring = True   Progressive spring instead of the instant hard clamp (see 2.4). OFF: when content hits the hard limit the camera snaps by exactly the overshoot, un-smoothed (a source of sudden pops).
hardSpringFastSmoothTime = 0.05   Smooth time AT the hard limit. DOWN: stiffer rubber band. UP: softer, content may stay nearer the edge for longer.

--- Look-ahead centre (opt-in) ---
smoothLookAheadCenter = True   Damp the CENTRE of the look-ahead box separately from its size, so a new corner entering the box drifts the frame instead of stepping it.
lookAheadCenterSmoothTime = 0.6   UP: very gentle drift toward new corners. DOWN: the frame centre reacts faster (more step-like).

--- Speed-scaled turn lead (opt-in) ---
speedScaledLead = True   Adds up to leadMaxExtraSegments to transitionLeadSegments as speed rises. leadMaxExtraSegments = 2 [0..3]: 0 extra below 25% of the speed range, 1 at 25-75%, 2 above 75%.
    UP (max extra): earlier moves at high speed. Effective lead stayed 0 in this recording (speed <= 16.7 u/s, 25% needs ~17.2).

--- Flip impact (opt-in) ---
flipImpactEnabled = False   TriggerFlipImpact() (called on a double-tap flip) is ignored. If ON: shakeMagnitude 0.4 world units for shakeDuration 0.15 s on the child camera, plus a punch-in of
    punchAmount (0 here, code default 1.5) for punchDuration 0.1 s, never below punchMinZoom 0.92 x zoom.


================================================================================================
6. EVERYTHING ELSE THAT CHANGES THE CAMERA
================================================================================================

6.1 DynamicPathGenerator (on the path generator object)  - camera-relevant values in this scene
    minSegmentsPerZone = 2, maxSegmentsPerZone = 3     random base size of a zone (= of a camera shot).
    targetZoneSeconds = 5, maxSegmentsPerZoneCap = 6   zone is stretched to last ~5 s at the runner's speed, up to 6 legs. DOMINANT lever on move size:
                                                       UP: fewer, bigger moves (shot centres further apart, 17-54 u). DOWN (e.g. 2-3): more frequent, smaller moves (limited by minHoldSeconds 2.5).
    minZonesAhead = 2, minSegmentsAhead = 6            sealed zones / legs always built ahead (the camera needs the current AND next shot solved).
    zonesToKeepBehind = 5                              zones kept behind the runner before their cubes are destroyed.
    boostSections = ON, minLegsBetweenBoosts 12, maxLegsBetweenBoosts 16 (profile waves override), boostLegCount 7, boostLegCubes 12, boostSpeedMultiplier 1.2
    boostCameraZoomOut = 1.15, boostCameraZoomInSeconds = 0.5, boostCameraZoomOutSeconds = 0.4
          while the runner is on a zig-zag boost the ortho is multiplied from 1 to 1.15 (linear, "InSeconds" 0.5 s = pulling back) and back (0.4 s).
          Rate = 0.15/0.5 = 0.30 per s going out, 0.15/0.4 = 0.375 per s coming back  ->  at ortho ~23.4 that is ~7 and ~8.8 ortho units/s (the FAST-ZOOM flags in the log).
          UP the zoom factor: bigger pull-back. UP the seconds: slower, calmer zoom (recommended if the zoom feels jumpy). (Profile overrides these at runtime.)
    portalZones = ON, legsBetweenPortals = 30, portalRunwayCubes 30, portalCameraYawOffset = 45  zone doors force the camera yaw on their two zones.
    legTiers (used when time-budget is off): 14-18 (from leg 0), 16-22 (16), 19-28 (36), 22-34 (66) cubes. firstLegMinCubes 20.
    pathClearance 3, turn weights left 2 / right 4 / up 1 / down 2 (reroll every 5 score): decide how far each leg goes and which way, i.e. how far apart consecutive shot centres are.
    difficultyProfile = MainScenePropCamera2_Difficulty.asset (assigned; see 6.2).

6.2 DifficultyProfile (asset assigned on the generator)  - camera section + what feeds it
    cameraOverrides = 1      -> speedZoomMax 1.15 (rig value = min(rig, 1.15)), boostZoom 1.15, boostZoomIn 0.5 s, boostZoomOut 0.4 s (overwrite the generator's values at start, runtime only).
    restrictCameraRotation = 1 -> yaw changes only into zones whose first leg is RELEASE phase or a portal runway.
    wavePacing = 1: 30-leg cycle; releaseEnd 5 (legs 0-5: RELEASE, camera may rotate), buildEnd 20, peakEnd 27, then cool-down to the portal. phaseLegs {15,60,150} = leg where onboarding ends / ramp ends / mastery ends (which leg-duration range applies).
    timeBudgetLegs = 1: leg lengths come from durations: onboarding 1.0-1.3 s, ramp 0.8-1.1 s, mastery 0.68-0.95 s, floor 0.62-0.9 s; firstLegSeconds 1.8. The faster the runner,
                        the more cubes per leg, so the 20-cube look-ahead cap covers less than one leg later on.
    useProfileSpeedCurve = 1: vStart 11.9 u/s growing toward its closing speed (recording: 11.9 -> 16.7 u/s over 31 s).
    fairInput / fairCorners / feedbackFX: runner input and feedback; they do not move the camera.

6.3 PathDepthShading (same object as the generator)  - decides what is drawn (section 4A) and gives VisibleAheadCubes to the rig
    visibleLegsAhead = 3, visibleLegsBehind = 2, edgeFadeCubes = 5, revealCubesPerSecond = 45, hideCubesPerSecond = 60, behindFadeOutCubes = 5, matchRunnerTrailToVisibleTrack = ON.
    UP visibleLegsAhead: more track drawn ahead and a bigger VisibleAheadCubes (the rig's minimum look-ahead rises toward lookAheadMaxCubes). DOWN: less drawn, rig minimum falls to lookAheadCubes 10.
    Also (look only): fullSizeAheadCubes 30, shrinkSpanCubes 25, farScale 0.6, opaqueAheadCubes 45, fadeSpanCubes 30 - cubes far ahead shrink and turn transparent, so track beyond ~30-45 cubes ahead is already
    small/faint even if it is on screen.

6.4 CubeRailRunner (the runner)  - what it contributes
    Runner position -> follow target and must-see box.  forwardSpeed -> hand-over time (distance/speed), speedFraction (speed zoom + lead).
    startSpeed 14 x overallSpeedMultiplier 0.85 = 11.9 u/s; maxSpeed 33; hardMaxSpeed 42; boost x1.2 on top. The camera's speed fraction uses the speed at Start as 0 and maxSpeed as 1.
    Flip (double-tap) -> TriggerFlipImpact (disabled here).  New leg -> reads cameraRig.SettledViewRotation to decide whether left/right must change.
    Soft restart -> SnapToPlayerZone + 0.4 s glide (CameraRewindSeconds = 0.4 constant).

6.5 GameOverSequence
    CameraDriftSeconds = 0.2: the camera follows the death arc for 0.2 s then the rig is disabled and the camera freezes; OverlayDelay 1.0 s, ShatterDelay 0.3 s.

6.6 Time
    DebugTimeScale: slowDown OFF. Time.timeScale = 1. All SmoothDamp / transition times above are in game seconds, frame-rate independent (the recording ran at ~180 fps in the editor).


================================================================================================
7. HOW THE RECORDING BELOW LINES UP WITH THE LOGIC (observations only, no changes made)
================================================================================================
  * 6 camera moves between score 0 and 25, each a pure PAN (yaw stayed 315.000): the yaw plan never asked for a turn and restrictCameraRotation allows turning only in RELEASE legs.
  * Each move starts when the runner steps onto the last leg of the zone (hold 3.5-4.4 s had already elapsed, minHold 2.5 s was not the limiting factor) and lasts 1.03-1.21 s.
  * The distance between consecutive shot centres was 17-54 world units (zones of ~4 legs). Over ~1.2 s that is an average 14-45 u/s of shot motion; the camera itself peaked at 26-64 u/s,
    against a runner speed of 12-17 u/s.
  * The rendered zoom did NOT follow the shot: zoomPeak stayed at 22.000 and ortho 23.1-27.2 the whole run while the zone ortho sizes were 35-89 (see 2.3). Only the camera POSITION moves.
  * Follow changes sign at each hand-off, partly cancelling and partly adding to the pan: e.g. move 1 the shot centre moved 21.8 u but the camera moved 18.3 u; move 4 the shot moved 44.7 u and the camera 40.1 u.
  * Boost (score 14 and 19) raised ortho 23.4 -> 27.0 in 0.5 s and back to 23.6 in 0.4 s (7-8.8 ortho/s). Move 5 began on the same frame the boost zoom started to come back.
  * Move 6 started with a one-frame 2.9 unit camera position step: baseBoom jumped 60 -> 62.88 (new zone's boom). Orthographic => the picture does not change, but it shows in the position column.
  * Static phases: the camera drifted at 5-6 u/s on average (0.41 x the runner's speed, matches followPlayer 0.45).
